title: The effect of promoting factors on learning by four different delivery modes
reason: RCT secondary analysis relating self-rated concentration, anticipation and liking (1-10 scales) to e-test scores across live, live-stream, vodcast and podcast teaching. The predictors are self-report, not platform-recorded indicators or activity products.

extraction.design: RCT secondary analysis (four delivery groups), regression and correlation
extraction.lms_indicators: none (Webropol e-test used only as outcome)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: short- and long-term e-test scores; self-reported concentration, anticipation, liking
extraction.notes: Full text is the Research Square preprint (DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-4075643/v1) of the BMC Med Educ article; title differs slightly ('four teaching methods'). n is the sum of high (200) and low (98) concentration groups in the short-term test (Table 3). Concentration (self-report) related to test score within groups, e.g. 'B 3.594, St.B 0.321, p = 0.01' - self-report ↔ achievement, not extracted as an indicator effect.
